body: Curaçao is a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, located north of western Venezuela in the Caribbean Sea, and is counted as part of the Netherlands for country streaks.
Curaçao uses square licence plates that appear completely white when blurred; front plates are usually mandatory but some vehicles lack them.
This black car with a roof rack is unique to Curaçao.
Due to its semi-arid climate, cacti are commonly seen in Curaçao.
Much of Curaçao’s architecture consists of simple, pastel-colored one-storey bungalows with metal roofs on smaller shacks and tiled roofs on larger houses; multi-storey villas are sometimes seen.
Road signs often have a colored border continuing onto the back, usually red or blue.
Blue street signs on top of yellow signposts are common in Curaçao.
White and black striped traffic light posts are found in urban areas.
Wooden poles with three horizontal alternating insulators are common, a style also found in Brazil, South Africa, and Eswatini.
The western half of Curaçao features a semi-arid rural landscape with green but dry hills and narrow roads; houses are spread apart.
A line of wind turbines can be seen at a wind farm in the southeast, with notably rainy coverage.
The Queen Juliana Bridge in Willemstad is a wide four-lane bridge with yellow and blue guardrails and a city view.
